topic.angle: Jenner's cowpox experiment and the idea behind every vaccine

panels.text: England, 1796. Edward Jenner suspects that people who catch cowpox, a much milder disease, are protected from smallpox.
On 14 May he takes pus from the cowpox blisters of a milkmaid, Sarah Nelmes, and inoculates James Phipps, an eight-year-old, through two small cuts.
Phipps gets a fever but no full-blown infection. On 1 July Jenner injects him with smallpox material, and again no disease follows.

That is the idea behind vaccines today: a harmless version of a germ teaches the immune system to recognise it, so it can destroy the real one later. The word vaccine comes from Jenner's Latin for cowpox.

probes.question: What does a vaccine do?
options: It kills the germs directly in the blood
It teaches the immune system to recognise a germ before the real infection
It swaps your white blood cells for new ones
It makes the body immune to every disease

probes.question: True or false: Jenner's 1796 experiment used cowpox material to protect against smallpox.

claims.claim: 1796 England: Jenner suspected cowpox sufferers were protected from smallpox; cowpox is much milder
claims.quote: Jenner postulated that the pus in blisters from sufferers of cowpox (a disease similar to smallpox but much less virulent) protected them from smallpox.

claims.claim: Jenner took pus from milkmaid Sarah Nelmes's cowpox blisters
claims.quote: Jenner scraped pus from cowpox blisters on the hands of Sarah Nelmes, a milkmaid who had caught cowpox from a cow called Blossom

claims.claim: On 14 May (1796) Jenner inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps
claims.quote: On 14 May 1796, he tested his hypothesis by inoculating James Phipps , the eight-year-old son of Jenner's gardener.

claims.claim: Inoculated through two small cuts; fever but no full-blown infection
claims.quote: Jenner inoculated Phipps through two small cuts on his arm that day; this led to a fever and some uneasiness, but no full-blown infection.

claims.claim: On 1 July Jenner injected smallpox material and no disease followed
claims.quote: On 1 July 1796, Jenner injected Phipps with variolous material , the routine method of immunisation at that time, and again no disease followed.

claims.claim: A vaccine teaches the immune system to recognise a germ so it can destroy it later (probe 1)
claims.quote: The agent stimulates the immune system to recognize the agent as a threat, destroy it, and recognize further and destroy any of the microorganisms associated with that agent that it may encounter in the future.

claims.claim: The word vaccine comes from Jenner's Latin for cowpox; 1796 cowpox experiment (probe 2)
claims.quote: The terms vaccine and vaccination are derived from Variolae vaccinae ("pustules of the cow"), the term devised by Jenner to denote cowpox .
